seed: Objects of type `block` under action ACTION4 with touching neighbours [arm] show mixed outcomes: no_change x10, x x4. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a global object such as a counter, HUD element or legend, read as state. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Crane game: ring+beam move y-/+6 (A1/A2), carrying blocks overlapping the beam and pushing any blocks they hit (chain). The whole move is cancelled if any block would leave y in [2,58].
A4/A3 change the beam width by +/-6 (range 1..43). Hooked (a next/collected block at x == tip-4) means blocks on the beam follow the tip. Unhooked, extending pushes blocks in the swept columns.
If the moved group would go past x>48 or into the ring, the beam changes width alone. Clicks, A5 and A7 do nothing.
Tags: a hooked next block alone on the beam becomes collected and the rightmost todo becomes next. An unhooked collected block reverts to next, and that next goes back to todo.
The block A4 mixed outcome is not a global counter (none exists): it is the chain hitting x>48 or the beam already at max width. The ring y bounds (0..58) are a guess. Stateless.
